items.title: Ministering—“That Ye Love One Another; as I Have Loved You”
items.speaker: By Sister Kristin M. Yee
items.speaker_role: Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
items.thumbnail_evidence: Exact posterFallback image URL decoded from the official message HTML; og:image used when no poster.

study_review.intro: Sister Yee describes ministering as personal, compassionate care patterned after Christ, including choosing to love when we cannot fix another person’s circumstances.
study_review.reflection_question: Who could I listen to or care for this week without assuming I must solve everything?
study_review.evidence_note: Her father’s ministering companions did not judge him; she expressly distinguishes loving service from fixing circumstances and emphasizes individual needs.
study_review.review_status: Full official message body read; intro supported; question is optional focusChrist application, not attributed speaker wording.

items.speaker: By Elder David A. Bednar

study_review.intro: Elder Bednar connects enduring valiantly with receiving charity and becoming more like Christ through His grace, rather than relying on determination alone.
study_review.reflection_question: Where could I seek the Savior’s help to become more loving, beyond simply completing a difficult responsibility?
study_review.evidence_note: The talk explains spiritual transformation, gifts as God-given rather than earned solely by discipline, charity, and gradual growth through Christ.

items.speaker_role: First Counselor in the First Presidency
items.thumbnail_evidence: Exact posterFallback image URL decoded from the official message HTML; og:image used when no poster.

study_review.intro: President Eyring teaches that sincere, continuing prayer invites the Lord’s peace and support through joyful seasons, uncertainty, and grief.
study_review.reflection_question: What would help me turn to Heavenly Father consistently, including when I do not know what to say?
study_review.evidence_note: The talk distinguishes heartfelt prayer from elaborate language, includes silent prayers, and encourages ongoing prayer in both joy and distress.

study_review.intro: President Uchtdorf invites us to seek a personal witness of the living Christ and share that witness through courageous, humble discipleship and service.
study_review.reflection_question: How could one humble act of service express my faith in the living Savior today?
study_review.evidence_note: The women at the empty tomb frame his invitation to gain a witness; later passages connect witness with everyday discipleship, love, and service.

study_review.intro: President Oaks connects faith in the Resurrection with daily discipleship, urging love for adversaries and peaceful language in family and other relationships.
study_review.reflection_question: Which conversation could I approach with greater respect and fewer harsh words?

items.title: Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey
items.speaker: By Elder Neil L. Andersen
items.speaker_role: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
items.thumbnail_evidence: Exact posterFallback image URL decoded from the official message HTML; og:image used when no poster.

study_review.intro: Elder Andersen describes eternal marriage as continuing growth in Christlike qualities, emphasizing covenants, patience, repentance, forgiveness, and reliance on the Holy Ghost.
study_review.reflection_question: Which Christlike quality could I practice more deliberately in a close relationship?
study_review.evidence_note: The talk presents marriage as spiritual development and an ongoing journey. It explicitly includes repentance, forgiveness, patience, and the Holy Ghost; it also acknowledges divorce and unmarried disciples.
